characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-199999): Iron Man 2 through Avengers: Endgame
characters.summary: Colonel James Rhodes, a U.S. Air Force officer and pilot, fights in a series of heavily armed War Machine suits (minigun, missile pods, shoulder cannon, stun baton, missile dispenser). Vanko once hijacked his suit, and Vision's errant blast caused the fall that left him paralyzed from the waist down.

techniques: Missile pods and the 'Ex-Wife' bunker buster

mechanisms: Armored suit with superhuman strength and durability (Mark VI)

weaknesses: The suit can be hijacked or stolen (Vanko took remote control; Savin stole the Iron Patriot armor)
Out of the suit he is paralyzed from the waist down and relies on leg braces
mobility: Armored flight (Mark VI 'possesses advanced flight capabilities')
limitations: All combat power comes from the armor
Mark VI pinned under rubble and abandoned when Thanos's ship bombarded the Avengers Compound

sources.supports: MCU War Machine: Air Force officer and pilot, armor marks and weapons (minigun, missiles, Mark III cannon and stun baton, Mark IV missile dispenser), Vanko hijack, Vision's blast and paralysis, Savin's theft of Iron Patriot
Mark VI: flight, strength and durability, built-in walking aid, Time Heist to Morag, abandoned under rubble after Sanctuary II's bombardment

unknowns: 'Energy shields (Mark VI/VII)', EMP vulnerability and jammed joints are not supported by the opened pages and were removed.
Repulsors and machine guns are listed on the Mark VI page without detail.
The Battle of Earth and the fight with Nebula are not described on the opened pages.

feats.claim: Used the Mark IV's missile dispenser extensively in the Battle of Wakanda.
Travelled through the Quantum Realm in the Mark VI to retrieve the Power Stone from Morag in 2014.

notableResults.note: After regaining control of his hijacked suit, he and Iron Man defeated the drones.
Vision's errant blast severely damaged the Mark III; Rhodes fell and was paralyzed from the waist down. Friendly fire, not a duel.

campaignTags.claim: Fights in advanced War Machine armor (owner ruling: Iron Man and War Machine armor earns tech).
The Mark VI armor 'possesses advanced flight capabilities'.
Suit weapons include a stun baton, missile pods and a missile dispenser.
A decorated U.S. Air Force pilot.

characters.summary: A.I.M. upgraded Rhodes's War Machine armor into the red, white and blue Iron Patriot, the U.S. military's weapon against the Ten Rings. An Extremis soldier subdued Rhodes in Pakistan, Savin stole the armor and used it to kidnap President Ellis, and Rhodes escaped Killian's mansion, rescued Ellis and reclaimed the suit.

mechanisms: Armored suit that stayed locked against Killian's men

weaknesses: Extremis heat forced him out of the armor
Lured by a hacked phone and subdued by a disguised Extremis soldier
limitations: The armor can be stolen and flown by someone else (Savin)
characters.formDifferences: War Machine Mark II armor upgraded by A.I.M. and repainted red, silver and blue as the government's Iron Patriot; shoulder gatling gun and concealed weapons.

sources.supports: Iron Patriot armor: A.I.M. upgrade, gatling gun, concealed weapons, repulsors, thruster boots, flight, Savin's theft, Rhodes rescuing Ellis and reclaiming it
Rhodes subdued by an Extremis soldier in Pakistan, tortured with Extremis heat, knocked out by Savin, armor stolen, Rhodes fights his way out

MCU War Machine: Air Force officer and pilot, armor marks and weapons (minigun, missiles, Mark III cannon and stun baton, Mark IV missile dispenser), Vanko hijack, Vision's blast and paralysis, Savin's theft of Iron Patriot

unknowns: The original 'remote override' weakness is not supported; the opened pages describe an ambush, Extremis heat and theft instead.
The Endgame Iron Patriot (War Machine Mark VII) is not covered here.

feats.claim: Fought his way out of Aldrich Killian's mansion after his capture.

notableResults.note: Subdued in his armor by a disguised Extremis soldier in Pakistan; Savin later knocked him unconscious and stole the suit.
Rhodes rescued President Ellis and reclaimed the armor (with Iron Man).

campaignTags.claim: Wears the A.I.M.-upgraded Iron Patriot armor.
Thruster boots; the armor flew Ellis to Killian's Miami base.
A decorated U.S. Air Force pilot.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-199999): Captain America: The Winter Soldier and Civil War
characters.summary: Bucky Barnes, brainwashed by Hydra into a super soldier with a Soviet metal arm, fought Steve Rogers on the highway and the Helicarrier, and later fought Tony Stark in Siberia, where Stark destroyed the arm.
weaknesses: Hydra trigger words make him obey whoever recites them (Zemo did so in 2016)
His metal arm can be destroyed (Stark in Siberia)
limitations: Brainwashing controls his actions until Shuri's cure

sources.supports: MCU Bucky: human cyborg super soldier with a metal arm, trigger words used by Zemo, highway and Helicarrier fights, Siberia fight with Stark

unknowns: The 'halted a moving vehicle with his arm' feat is not on the opened page and was removed.
Removed the 'stealth' tag: owner ruling requires a documented stealth feat, and an assassin role is not enough.

notableResults.note: Fought Rogers on the highway and on the third Helicarrier; Rogers completed his mission and Barnes pulled him from the Potomac.
Team result in Siberia: Stark destroyed Barnes's arm, and Rogers disabled Stark's armor.

campaignTags.claim: Described as a 'human cyborg' with a metal arm.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics Earth-616, Captain America vol. 5 #34 (2008) onward through Fear Itself, comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: After Steve Rogers's death, Bucky takes up the shield at Tony Stark's choosing, carrying a pistol and a Fury-built bionic arm with an EMP ability. His tenure ends after Sin stabs him in Fear Itself and he fakes his death to return to covert work.
weaknesses: Rash tactics: he often rushes in, gets captured and needs allies to rescue him
limitations: Not serum-enhanced to Steve Rogers's level; the bionic arm is what lets him throw the shield properly
characters.formDifferences: Bucky in the Captain America role: Cap's shield plus a gun and a Fury-built bionic arm with an EMP ability, which replaced the Soviet arm.

sources.supports: Captain America (2004) series: Bucky's shield, pistol and EMP bionic arm, tactics, Sin's stabbing in Fear Itself, faked death
2008 announcement: Bucky Barnes becomes Captain America with the shield, a gun and a new uniform

unknowns: The original record used MCU events (Civil War airport shield catch, the Iron Man fight); those belong to the MCU Winter Soldier and were removed from this comics form.
Fights with the Grand Director, Zemo and Master Man are not detailed on the opened pages.

feats.claim: One of only two non-serum-enhanced characters able to throw Cap's shield properly, thanks to his bionic arm.

notableResults.note: She stabbed him with her hammer and he seemed to die; he survived and faked his death.

conditional.dependsOn: Captain America's shield and his bionic arm

campaignTags.claim: Bionic arm with an EMP ability, built by Nick Fury.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-199999): Avengers: Infinity War onward (Wakandan cure and the White Wolf name), Endgame, The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
characters.summary: Cured by Shuri and named White Wolf in Wakanda, Bucky fights with a vibranium arm. He joined the Battle of Wakanda and the final battle in Endgame, beat thugs in Madripoor, and with Sam Wilson broke John Walker's arm.
weaknesses: Ayo's Wakandan failsafe can deactivate his vibranium arm
limitations: The vibranium arm is Wakandan-made and can be shut off by the Dora Milaje
characters.formDifferences: Post-cure Bucky: Hydra trigger words nullified by Shuri, and a Wakandan vibranium arm instead of the Soviet one.

sources.supports: MCU Bucky: Shuri's cure and the White Wolf name, vibranium arm, Battle of Wakanda, Endgame, Madripoor bar fight, Ayo's failsafe, the fight with Walker

unknowns: 'Vibranium arm EMP pulse' is not supported for the MCU arm and was removed; the EMP arm belongs to the comics version.
The original 'Outriders: win' was changed to a feat: Thanos won the Battle of Wakanda.

feats.claim: Fought in the Battle of Wakanda before being among the first to disintegrate in the Blip.

notableResults.citation: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
notableResults.note: Pretended to be under mind control, then defeated them.

notableResults.citation: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
notableResults.note: Team result with Sam Wilson in the fight over the shield; they broke Walker's arm.

notableResults.citation: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
notableResults.note: Her failsafe deactivated his vibranium arm.
Team result in the final battle.

campaignTags.claim: A 'human cyborg' with a Wakandan vibranium arm.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics Earth-616, Ghost Rider/Wolverine: Weapons of Vengeance (2023), Omega #1; temporary possession, comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: Weapon Plus bound the demon Bagra-ghul to a captured Logan, making a mind-controlled killer with Wolverine's healing factor, hellfire-wreathed adamantium claws and a flaming skull. He hunted mutants for them until Bagra-ghul was exorcised and defeated.
weaknesses: Controlled through a Weapon Plus mind-control helmet
The demon can be exorcised from him
limitations: Temporary: Bagra-ghul was exorcised by the end of the story
characters.formDifferences: Logan fused with the demon Bagra-ghul: hellfire claws and a flaming skull on top of his healing factor.

sources.supports: Hellverine in Weapons of Vengeance Omega #1: Weapon Plus binds Bagra-ghul to Logan, healing factor plus hellfire, flaming claws and skull, mind-control helmet, kills mutant terrorists, fights Ghost Rider, demon exorcised

unknowns: The original 'holy magic' weakness is not supported and was removed.
Whether this form has a penance stare or other Ghost Rider powers is not stated.

feats.claim: Killed a group of mutant terrorists while controlled by Weapon Plus.
feats.citation: Ghost Rider/Wolverine: Weapons of Vengeance Omega #1

notableResults.citation: Ghost Rider/Wolverine: Weapons of Vengeance Omega #1
notableResults.note: Killed them on Weapon Plus's orders.

notableResults.citation: Ghost Rider/Wolverine: Weapons of Vengeance Omega #1
notableResults.note: After the Ghost Rider fight, Bagra-ghul was exorcised from Logan and defeated; the page doesn't say who struck the decisive blow.

campaignTags.claim: His adamantium claws are wreathed in hellfire.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics Earth-807128, Wolverine #66-72 and Giant-Size Old Man Logan (2008-2009), alternate future, comics form (not the 2017 film Logan)
characters.summary: Decades after Mysterio tricked him into killing the X-Men, Logan refuses to pop his claws and lives as a farmer in a villain-ruled wasteland. On a cross-country job with blind Hawkeye he beheads President Red Skull with Cap's shield, and after the Hulk gang kills his family he becomes Wolverine again and takes bloody revenge.
weaknesses: His vow never to pop his claws: he let the Hulk gang beat him in front of his family
mobility: On foot; drove the old Spider-Mobile cross-country
limitations: Self-imposed refusal to fight until his family is killed
characters.formDifferences: An aged, alternate-future Logan who stopped fighting after Mysterio tricked him into killing the X-Men; his healing factor still works.

sources.supports: Wolverine #66-72 and Giant-Size Old Man Logan: Mysterio's trick, refusing to fight the Hulk gang, the trip with Hawkeye, beheading Red Skull with Cap's shield, revenge on the Hulk gang, recovering from injuries

unknowns: The original record described the 2017 film Logan (adamantium poisoning, Reavers); that is a different continuity and was removed.
The final fight with Bruce Banner is not described on the opened page.

feats.claim: Recovered after being blasted in New Babylon and beheaded President Red Skull with Captain America's shield.
Survived putting his head on the tracks until a train smashed into him.

notableResults.note: Cut off his head with Captain America's shield.
After they killed his family, he took bloody revenge.
Earlier, he refused to fight back and was beaten in front of his family.
Mysterio's illusion tricked him into killing all of the X-Men.

campaignTags.claim: Healed after the beating and after being blasted in New Babylon.
